title: Multi-select — multiple correct answers
description: Three multi-select Quiz widgets covering the partial-credit shape: "all correct" required for `done`, but per-option ✓/✗ feedback shows the user which picks were wrong.

data.markdown: When `multiSelect: true`, the widget renders checkbox semantics: any subset of options can be selected. The `correct` array lists every option index that should be checked. Submission is graded as **all correct or nothing** — picking three of four correct options is still a wrong submission. Per-option ✓/✗ feedback (US-057) helps the user see which picks were off.

data.question: Which of the following are widget types in the Quiz/Theory/Code family registered in `widgetRegistry`? (Pick every option that is true.)
data.explanation: Theory and Quiz are explanatory/assessment widgets. Histogram and PlotImage are visualization widgets — distinct family. All four are valid widget types overall, but the question scoped to the Quiz/Theory/Code family.

data.question: Pick every statement that is true about the Quiz widget's grading model.
options: A multi-select submission is correct only when the picked set exactly matches `correct`.
The explanation panel renders only after the user submits.
A correct submission marks the section as `done: true` in `progress.json`.
The widget runs Python tests against the user's answer.
The user can change their answer freely after submitting.
data.explanation: Grading is exact-match on the selected indices. The explanation reveals on submit, and a fully-correct submission persists the section as done. The Quiz widget never runs Python — that is the Code/Sandbox/ParametricExplorer family — and the form locks on submit rather than allowing free re-answering.

sections.title: All five correct (every option is right)

data.question: Which of these are valid Markdown features inside a Theory widget? (Pick every option that is true.)
options: Fenced code blocks with language hints
data.explanation: All five are supported. The Theory widget pipeline is `react-markdown` + `remark-math` + `rehype-katex` + `remark-directive` + `remarkCallout`, so anything documented in those plugins works.
